figures.caption: Repeat-flow primary results: circles show weighted empirical median absolute pair differences and bars the weighted interquartile range, not a confidence interval. Grey dots show each observed window median. Only successful adjacent-position pairs with actual start lag75–125ms in common cells are represented. Windows/cells/classes use the frozen conditional weights. UU and DD are same-mode repeatability controls; DU is cross-mode separation. Runs remain separate and no jitter subtraction identifies causal encryption cost.

All four predeclared sensitivity thresholds for repeat-flow primary pairs. Rates use the same common-cell/window weights as the median comparison and need not equal a pooled integer count divided by pair count. They describe dependent observed pairs under the selected lag condition, not population probabilities, equivalence or user-perception limits. No cross-run pooling occurs.

Repeat-flow weighted median magnitudes under primary adjacent75–125ms lags, all adjacent lags, tight adjacent90–110ms lags, and position separations2/3 within75–125%of their target lag. Each view recomputes common overlap and therefore can condition on a different set of cells; sample counts are retained. Lines only connect descriptive summaries. Missing overlap produces gaps, never an imputed estimate.

Separate-run weighted primary median absolute differences for same-mode DoH repeats (DD) and DoH-versus-UDP pairs (DU), under the same versus distinct prepared-flow rules. Both provider panels share the x scale. Matching and weighting are identical to the full results: adjacent successful pairs, actual start lag75–125ms, common position/domain/window cells and equal window mass. Points are descriptive estimates without confidence intervals; distinct flows do not establish independent routes. No cross-run pooling or jitter subtraction.

Weighted median absolute pair differences and interquartile ranges under repeated or distinct prepared flows, in the same primary position/lag stratum. Distinct UDP/H2 objects and source ports are not assumed statistically independent or separate physical paths. Between-flow level differences and temporal variation can both contribute. Bars are IQRs, not uncertainty intervals for a population estimate.
